subject: Private deployment — detailed offline upgrade / supply-chain / operator controls
messages:
From: Carly Jacobs <carly.jacobs@healtech.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healtech.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're working through the security and procurement review for a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment and hit a few questions specific to offline/air-gapped scenarios. Can you provide detailed, itemized answers for the following:

- How Redwood performs signed upgrades in an environment with no egress (supply chain attestation, signed artifacts, verification procedure).
- SBOM availability and how we can validate component provenance locally.
- Operator access model for on-prem operators (SAML/LDAP integration when there is no IdP connectivity; support for offline local accounts).
- Emergency patching process (how we distribute urgent fixes into an air-gapped customer site; what evidence you provide).
- Backup/restore and disaster recovery for KV caches / model artifacts in isolated networks.

We'd like a written response plus any runbooks or diagrams you can share (we can treat those as restricted attachments). Procurement has asked for these before we finalize the SOW.

Appreciate a response by end of week if possible.

Best,
Carly Jacobs
Head of Infrastructure Security
HealTech Medical Systems

Thanks,

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Vanessa / Irene — forwarding HealTech's questions (see below). Key asks we should answer in the RFI doc: signed upgrade flow, SBOM verification offline, IdP-less operator auth, emergency patch airgap delivery, and DR for caches/model artifacts.

Notes for the response (draft bullets):
- Upgrades: artifact signing via RedSig (our signing service). We provide signed tarballs + detached signatures; in air-gapped installs we provide an offline signing verification tool (verify_signed_release.sh) and a signed manifest. Need to include exact checksum algorithm and verification steps.
- SBOM: we provide CycloneDX CSV export + a static notarized SBOM file (signed by our build pipeline). Customers can validate by checking the signature with our public key.
- Operator auth: we support local operator accounts with RBAC scoping; for SAML when IdP is unreachable we have a config mode for pre-seeded assertions and a rescue admin token stored in the customer's HSM.; need legal input on token storage wording.
- Emergency patching: process is pull-based (we generate an air-gap bundle and customer ingests via secure transport), or vendor-assisted courier for very large sites. Evidence: signed release notes, COSIGN signatures, and a signed attestation PDF.
- DR: KV cache snapshots and model artifacts can be exported to encrypted tarballs; we document restore order (model binaries, index files, KV snapshot) and recommend incremental snapshot cadence.

Irene — can you draft the operator runbook sections and list exact files we will attach (SBOM, runbook, network diagram)? Vanessa — can you confirm compliance language we include around notarized SBOM and signature verification?

Jonas
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Jonas / Vanessa — draft attached (internal). I added the step-by-step verification examples for the upgrade path and an operator checklist for air-gapped installs. Highlights:

- Signed upgrades: include example cosign verification commands, manifest structure (release-id, timestamp, SHA256 of artifacts), and a recommended local verification policy that customers can encode into their operator gate.
- SBOM: attach CycloneDX CSV and instructions to run `verify-sbom.sh` (script checks signature and component hashes).
- Operator accounts: documented three modes — connected SAML, pre-seeded local accounts with salted hashed passwords, and HSM-sealed rescue token. We've included recommended password rotation windows and operator access audit events.
- Emergency patching: prepared a templated attestation that engineering will fill when sending the air-gap bundle. Also included a checklist for escorted courier receipt (checksum verification, chain of custody log).

Attachments I'm preparing: operator_runbook_healtech.odt, sbom_redwood_2026.csv, deployment_network_diagram.pdf. I'll hand them to Jonas for redaction if needed.

Irene
Lead Installability Engineer
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Carly Jacobs <carly.jacobs@healtech.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healtech.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Carly — attached is our consolidated RFI response and supporting artifacts. Short summary of the key points follows; full details are in the attachments.

1) Signed upgrades (air-gapped):
- We deliver signed release bundles (tar.gz) with COSIGN and RedSig detached signatures.
- Customers validate signatures locally using our verify_signed_release.sh script (included).
- Release manifest includes release-id, build timestamp, checksums (SHA256), and our CI signature.

2) SBOM & provenance:
- We provide CycloneDX SBOM (CSV) and a notarized SBOM file signed by our CI.
- Customers can run verify-sbom.sh to validate signatures and component hashes without network access.

3) Operator access model (offline):
- Three supported modes: full IdP (SAML/OIDC), pre-seeded local operator accounts (salted hash), and HSM-sealed rescue tokens.
- Local accounts can be constrained with RBAC policies and local audit events are logged to the operator audit file.

4) Emergency patching & rollback:
- For critical fixes we produce an air-gap bundle plus a signed attestation PDF and step-by-step installer.
- Rollback: we publish explicit rollback artifacts (previous release bundle + manifest) and include a dry-run verification step.

5) Backup/DR for model artifacts & KV:
- We recommend nightly encrypted snapshots (configurable cadence) and provide a deterministic restore order. Snapshot/restore scripts are included in the runbook.

Attachments (attached): healtech_rfi_answers_v1.pdf (full answers), sbom_redwood_2026.csv, operator_runbook_healtech.odt, deployment_network_diagram.pdf

If you'd like, we'll hold a 30-minute call Friday 10/16 at 2:00pm PST to walk the engineering team through the emergency patch and rollback demo.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RE: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Jonas — thanks, the package looks thorough. A couple of follow-ups from engineering:

- In the emergency patching doc you describe a courier workflow. For our regulated sites the customer cannot accept physical media from vendors. Can you confirm the pull-based transfer process and whether we can sign the transport manifest into our own company KMS before ingestion?
- For the HSM-sealed rescue token: can you provide the exact token format and interoperability requirements (we run AWS CloudHSM on some sites and Thales on others)?

Procurement also asked if the notarized SBOM can be included as a separate signed artifact for the contract appendix.

Can we keep the 10/16 call; we'll invite our install and security SMEs.

— Carly
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Carly Jacobs <carly.jacobs@healtech.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: HealTech RFI — offline upgrade / operator controls follow-up

Carly — quick answers below; we can run the technical deep-dive on Friday as planned.

- Pull-based transfer: yes — we build an air-gap bundle and sign a transport manifest. Customers can re-sign the manifest with their KMS prior to ingestion; our ingestion tool validates both our signature and the customer signature. We'll include an example workflow and a sample script that performs the double-sign/validate step.

- HSM-sealed rescue token: token is a PKCS#7 envelope containing an AES-256 key blob plus an associated metadata header (release-id, expiry). We support export/import wrappers for AWS CloudHSM and PKCS#11-compatible HSMs (Thales, Entrust). We'll include a short interoperability matrix and example PKCS#11 commands in the runbook.

- Notarized SBOM: yes — we'll provide the notarized SBOM as a separate signed artifact suitable for contract appendices (PDF + detached signature).

I'll bring engineering on the call to demo the pull ingestion and token unwrap flow. Thanks for the quick turnaround on scheduling; please send the invite and we'll share the Zoom link and draft agenda.

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
